# INNO-TREC

Visual identity for the INNO-TREC project. The source is the INNO-TREC Brand Manual (`assets/Brand_Manual_INNOTREC.pdf`, 12 pages). Values marked "sampled" in a token's note were read from the manual's layout; values marked "proposed" are not in the manual and can be changed.

## Name

- Write the project name as **INNO-TREC** in running text.
- **INNOTREC** (no hyphen) appears only inside the logo. Never retype it in Corpta or any other font to imitate the logo; place a logo file instead.

## Logo

The logo is the symbol (a split disc with an outer arc and radial bars; the circles stand for the project's themes) plus the logotype INNOTREC. Their relationship is fixed.

| File | Layout | Colour | Use on |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `assets/Logos/logo-landscape-colour.png` | Horizontal: symbol + logotype | Full colour | `surface`, `surface-muted`, `green-tint`, `light-blue-tint` |
| `assets/Logos/logo-landscape-grey.png` | Horizontal | Greys (`logo-grey`, `logo-grey-light`) | Dark grounds (`ink`, `black`) |
| `assets/Logos/logo-curved-colour.png` | Symbol with logotype curved round the left | Full colour | Light grounds, as above |
| `assets/Logos/logo-curved-grey.png` | Same, curved | Greys | Dark grounds |
| `assets/Logos/logo-vertical-colour.png` | Symbol with logotype set vertically on the left | Full colour | Light grounds |
| `assets/Logos/logo-vertical-grey.png` | Same, vertical | Greys | Dark grounds |
| `assets/Logos/logo-stacked-colour.png` | Stacked: symbol above logotype | Full colour | Light grounds |
| `assets/Logos/logo-stacked-grey.png` | Same, stacked | Greys | Dark grounds |

- Use the full-colour ("dark") version on light grounds and the greyscale ("light") version on dark grounds.
- **Clearspace:** keep a margin of logo height ÷ 4 on all four sides free of any other element.
- The manual's do's and don'ts, verbatim:
  1. Do not place the logo type on 1 line
  2. Do not invert the logo symbol
  3. Do not alter the logo symbol
  4. Do not alter the logo type style
  5. Do not change the size relationship between the logo symbol and logo type.
  6. Never change the proportions of the logo vertically or horizontally or alter the appearance in any way
- In practice: use the files as supplied, scale them proportionally, and never recolour or redraw them.

## EU funding emblem

INNO-TREC is funded by Horizon Europe (grant agreement 101230578), so its outputs show the EU emblem with the statement "Funded by the European Union". The files are the official English horizontal set from the European Commission's logo download centre.

| File | Colour | Use on |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `assets/Funding/eu-funded-colour.png` | Full colour, blue text | Light grounds (`surface`, `surface-muted`) |
| `assets/Funding/eu-funded-negative.png` | Full colour flag with a white border, white text | Dark grounds (`ink`, `black`); the Footer uses it |

- Use the files as supplied: never recolour, crop, redraw or merge the emblem with other graphics or text. Use the colour versions; the monochrome versions in the official set are for media without colour.
- Make the emblem at least as large as the biggest other logo beside it.
- Put the full funding statement next to it. The Footer component carries the statement used on inno-trec.eu.

## Colour

Three brand colours, each tied to a project theme:

| Token | Manual name | Energy sector | Community | Tech |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `green` `#78b948` | Renewables | Renewables, sustainability | Growth, together | Modern tech, innovation |
| `light-blue` `#1978b8` | Digital platforms | Clean energy | Trust, connection | Digital platforms, data |
| `orange` `#ef7d1c` | Community | Warmth, energy flow | Community, inclusion | Energy, activity |

- Lead with `green` and `light-blue`; they carry the logo. Use `orange` as the accent.
- Set text in `ink` on `surface`, `surface-muted`, `green-tint`, `light-blue-tint` or `stone`.
- `light-blue` is the only brand colour that works as text on `surface` (4.75:1). Never set text in `green` or `orange` on light grounds; both fail contrast.
- On brand fills, use the matching `on-` token: `on-green` (= `ink`), `on-light-blue` (white), `on-orange` (black). The manual shows white labels on green and orange; those pairs fail contrast (2.4:1 and 2.8:1) and should not be copied for text.
- Use `surface-muted` for header bands, like the manual's running header, and as the app background behind cards.
- Interface colours (proposed): `ink-muted` for secondary text, `line` for dividers, `line-strong` for control borders, `focus` for the 2px focus ring, `danger`/`danger-tint` for errors and failed transactions, `orange-tint` behind warnings.
- Status always carries a word and an icon as well as a colour: active/certified `success`, measured/information `info`, estimated/warning `warning`, suspended/error `danger`.
- A balance below zero is not an error: community and dependent wallets are normally below zero. Show it with a minus sign in `ink`, never in `danger`.

## Typography

- **Figtree Bold** (`display` family) is the primary font: headings, titles, labels in capitals. Styles: `display`, `title`, `heading`.
- **Open Sans** (`text` family) is the secondary font, in Light and Bold: body text and tables. Styles: `body`, `body-light`, `label`, `caption`.
- **Corpta** is the logotype font only. Do not set any text in it.
- Both Figtree and Open Sans are free Google Fonts; load them from Google Fonts.
- Set section titles in capitals, as the manual does ("PROJECT COLOR SYSTEM").

## Layout

- Corners are square (`radius-none`) for blocks, panels and buttons.
- Mark a section label with a short `green` rule above it, as the manual does throughout.
- Space with `space-1`, `space-2`, `space-4`, `space-8`.

## Writing for members

Most members have little experience with digital tools. Member screens follow these rules; manager and administrator screens may show more detail.

- Use plain words: "credits", "send", "exchange for money", "community manager". Do not show "EC", "wallet ID", "purpose code", "issuance", "CEMA", hashes or identifiers outside "Technical details".
- One task per screen, one `primary` button, label it with a verb ("Send credits").
- Split tasks into short steps with "Step 1 of 3" and a Back button; always show a check step before anything moves, and a clear result after.
- Choose people from a list; never ask a member to type an ID or address.
- Pair every icon with words, and every colour with words and an icon.
- Text at least 16px, inputs and buttons at least 52px tall on member screens, rows at least 60px.
- Errors say what happened and what to do next, in one sentence. After a failed send, say that no credits moved.
- Never show formulas, conversion factors or rule names to members. The backend computes every credit amount; the interface only displays it.

## Components

React 18 components under the global `InnoTrec` (load React and ReactDOM 18, then `components/bundle.css` and `components/bundle.js`). `bundle.css` loads Figtree and Open Sans from Google Fonts. Data names follow the ECMS Technical Specification v1.0 (`assets/ECMS_Technical_Specification (V1).docx`).

- **Member screens:** `WalletBalance`, `BalanceStatement`, `EnergySummary`, `TransactionList`, `TransactionDetail`, `RecipientPicker`, `TransferForm`, `SettlementRequestForm`.
- **Manager screens:** `AccountCard`, `AccountList`, `StatTile`, `DataTable`, `Identifier`, `ConfidenceBadge`, `PurposeTag` (technical mode).
- **Shared:** `Button`, `TextField`, `Select`, `Card`, `Badge`, `InlineAlert`, `Icon`, `PurposeTag`.
- **Shell:** `TopBar`, `SideNav`, `AppShell`.

Rules that apply to all of them:

- Components display what the backend reports and collect input. Valuation, limits, balance rules, eligibility, signing and recording are the backend's job.
- Write amounts with their unit, with + or − in activity lists. Members see "credits"; managers see "EC".
- Ledger records are final once written: there is no "pending" or "failed" transaction. Requests that wait for the community manager (exchanging credits for money) are shown as requests, not as transactions.
- Open questions about the specification are listed in the section "Open questions"; components do not take a position on them.
- Each component's README lists the props it needs.
